free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Metered per slice: 'Each storage VPS slice adds 1TB SATA storage, 2GB memory, 2TB transfer'. A 2:1 ratio. At 10 slices = 10 TB storage and only 20 TB/mo transfer. Below the 30 TB/mo serving requirement. Overage rate not published on the page.

limits_note: Slice count adds RAM and cores linearly, which is wasted spend for pure storage. 10 Gbps shared port. The traffic ratio is the binding constraint, not the price.
reliability_note: Established US hosting provider in Secaucus and Los Angeles. Storage VPS pricing scales linearly at $3 per TB monthly.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

evidence.proved: 'Starts at $3.00 per TB per month'; 1 Slice $3/mo (1TB SATA, 2TB transfer, 10Gbps shared); 10 Slices $30/mo (10TB SATA, 20TB transfer); 20 Slices listed
same page — 'Use storage-optimized cloud compute for backups, archives, and high-volume file hosting when capacity matters more than raw application I/O'

price_per_tb_month: $3.00/TB/mo flat at 1, 5, 10, 20 TB — genuinely linear, no tier discount. Caveat: 2 TB transfer per TB stored does not cover 30 TB/mo serving at 20 TB stored (40 TB included, so it does at 20 TB; it fails at 10 TB stored where only 20 TB is included).
